prompts.text: Bounded: instrument the FIRST LAP and find why the ring never starts. Four candidate causes given with signatures. Do not redesign.

quarantine_reason: THE RING NOW RUNS. Remaining gap is FOUR WORDS, counted: the drain must run 4 laps with a plain rotate between them (8 of 32 words emit today); the rotate must come from the only cell reaching all four rows on one walk (wbk at (1,0)) and the lap must close via wb or seq, because the tap line and finish row run ONE-WAY AWAY from the control corner (measured, all four faces, every tap/adder/egress). Cost 5+3+6 words, 4 short even after compressing wbk's realignment 12->8 jumps behaviour-identically. LAYER: block program / fold word budget.
notes:
=== PASS 4 (2026-08-30) -- THE RING RUNS. It was candidate cause #2, five times over. ===

THE ANSWER TO THE DISPATCH QUESTION: not a missing HALT, not boot ordering. It was INV-48 root cause C -- A FACE THAT MISSES -- in five different disguises, with INV-50 as the accomplice that let all five hide.

WHAT NOW WORKS, ON THE REAL PLACED+ROUTED+BUILT CHIP, from the execution trace and the emitted words: exactly 80 quarter-round invocations through all sixteen reused stages; 19 half-boundary realignments; 37/38/39 realignment spins of rows 1/2/3; all four taps armed; and STATE WORD 0 BIT-EXACT (0xE4E7 0xF110, RFC 8439 S2.3.2), as is most of word 15. A wrong 20-round permutation cannot produce those bytes, so the datapath, the write-back, the fixed tap and the realignment are CONFIRMED ON SILICON.

THE FIVE DEFECTS. (1) Four cells carried is_face constants naming the wrong direction outright. ONE of them -- wbk's row-trigger face NORTH, off the top of the array -- IS the whole of 'the ring never starts': wbk had ZERO trace events. (2) THE FACE REGISTER PERSISTS ACROSS ENTRIES; two cells flipped and never restored, so the next entry fired in the last one's direction. (3) A CELL'S FLIP ALSO DEFLECTS WORDS THAT MERELY TRANSIT IT: wb sits on seq's walk and left itself pointing north, so every lap-start trigger bounced back into seq -- the ring did exactly ONE lap then ping-ponged forever. (4) An internal edge (in0.trig -> in1.default) was never declared. (5) THE BIG ONE: the router faced tap3 at its ADDER, walked that face, found tap3->add3->out->in0 and sized tap3.q->in0 at THREE hops; the word actually leaves EAST and overshot by two, so EVERY FRAME REACHED THE COLLECTOR TWO WORDS SHORT and the cipher ran five laps and stalled. That single edge was worth 75 of the 80 laps.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT GENERALISES (new INV-NEXT). Over all 233 internal edges: RESTING-face emits 211 correct / 0 wrong; FLIPPED-face emits 16 correct / 6 WRONG -- and all 16 'correct' ones are right ONLY BY COINCIDENCE (the resting walk missed, Manhattan fired, Manhattan happened to match; every one is a straight-line hop of 1 or 2). That is INV-50's real shape, and the spurious-success case is WORSE than the Manhattan fallback because nothing looks anomalous.

TWO TOOLCHAIN FIXES, BOTH REGRESSION-TESTED AT 1219 WITH ORIENTATION GREEN. router._place_block_cells looked programs up by the raw positional INDEX, False for every STRING-KEYED block -- so such a block never had its declared fwd_face honoured at all; now keyed by position. And _get_routing_distance takes an optional start_face, with blocks able to declare emit_faces() -> {(cell,port): neighbour_id}. The value is a CELL ID, not a direction, so the face is derived from PLACED coordinates and the declaration is orientation-correct BY CONSTRUCTION -- which is precisely what the previous by-hand-rotation attempt got wrong.

METHOD, building on the last pass's lesson. 'A model that flatters the design is worse than no model' needed a second turn of the screw: reading MOVE [FACE] out of the real programs is necessary but NOT sufficient. The checker must symbolically execute every path over both sides of every branch and iterate the face register TO A FIXPOINT -- seed with the resting face, collect what each path can LEAVE BEHIND, re-seed, repeat. A checker that assumes each entry starts clean cannot see defects 2 or 3, and those were half the bugs.

WHAT REMAINS: four words. The drain must run four laps with a plain rotate between them; the rotate must come from the only cell reaching all four rows on one walk (wbk at (1,0)) and the lap must be closed by one of the only two cells that can reach wbk, because the tap line and the finish row run ONE-WAY AWAY from the control corner (measured, all four faces, every tap/adder/egress). Cost 5+3+6 words; available 4 short even after compressing wbk's realignment 12 jumps -> 8.

TRAP FOR THE NEXT PASS, which cost the last hour: freeing one of those words by dropping seq's redundant 'MOVE half, four' FITS AND BREAKS THE BLOCK. Shortening seq moves seq.step's entry from 15 to 14 and the build then mis-resolves wbk.back to it instead of row0.pub (also 15) -- the realignment ran perfectly and handed control to the lap counter, and the ring died at the first boundary with a flawless trace. Entry addresses are params-dependent (INV-6/11) and that reaches INTERNAL edges: re-read the BUILT words, not just the budget.

HONESTY NOTE: still not done, and deliberately not marked so. It emits a quarter of its output. But the remaining defect is now a counted word budget on a named cell trio, not 'it does not compute'.

THE HEADLINE: THE SELECTOR WAS UNNECESSARY. The previous pass's architecture (8 lane cells, LOAD-indirect read, 4-way CMP/BR write-back, fan-out-8 selector broadcast, 8-cell demux) is replaced by a FIXED-TAP RING. Reading the schedule as a per-row READ OFFSET rather than as index(k)=4k+((j+k*shift)&3) collapses it: row k reads offsets 0,1,2,3 in the column half and k,k+1,k+2,k+3 in the diagonal half, so EVERY row taps SLOT 0 provided it rotates left by one after each quarter round, and the diagonal half is the same walk started k positions later (bracketed by k extra rotations and 4-k to restore alignment; a 4-slot rotation has order 4 so the brackets cancel). The tap is a CONSTANT and the whole permutation is a SHIFT REGISTER.

Proven EXACT against RFC 8439 S2.3.2 (state + the 64 keystream bytes) and S2.4.2 (the full 114-byte two-block encryption vector) over the same cell-level operations the hardware performs, with 8 INV-4 mutants. FOUR of those mutants -- diagonal-half-first, no-realignment, reversed spin direction, stuck tap -- ALL still perform exactly 80 invocations, so no count-based or structural check catches any of them. Same class as the counter-direction mutant found in attempt 2.

MEASURED ON THE REAL CHIP: (1) the row cell -- publish the head pair, install a written-back replacement, rotate four 32-bit slots -- correct on silicon, 4 spins the identity, 16 instructions with 5 spare words; (2) INV-48's forwarding rule watched LIVE as a failure and then a fix (a cell whose resting face misses its target gives NO output and NO error; an in-program FACE flip fixes it); (3) a word TRANSITS cells carrying a FACE and NO PROGRAM at distances 2/3/4/6 -- but the build faces a bare array cell only where a ROUTE claims it, so a gap inside a block's OWN footprint is still a dead end for a block-internal WRITE.

NEW SILENT TRAP FOUND AND GATED -- POSITIONAL PAIRING (INV-33/INV-50): build_cell_programs and default_layout must ITERATE IN THE SAME ORDER, because the router and build walk the programs and the placed cells in lockstep BY POSITION. Both dicts are keyed by cell id, which HIDES the mismatch: the design places, routes, builds and DRCs clean while whole cells come out with EMPTY memory. Cost one debug cycle here.

NEW INV-50 (three mechanisms, all silent): a CLOSED RING TRAPS ITS INTERIOR (every ring cell forwards along the ring, so nothing emitted inside can ever leave -- measured over all 26 rotations and four emit directions; fold as a serpentine, not a ring, whenever an interior cell must reach an edge); the positional-pairing contract; and the gap/transit asymmetry above.

METHOD NOTE: the fold-search checker initially credited a FACE flip to any cell I nominated, and passed a layout that then mis-resolved on silicon -- a flip only exists if the cell's PROGRAM contains MOVE [FACE]. Rewriting the checker to read the programs turned three 'green' edges red immediately. A model that flatters the design is worse than no model.

=== PASS 3 (2026-08-29/30) — architecture REPLACED and simplified ===

THE PRIOR PASS'S PLAN WAS UNNECESSARY. It had 8 lane cells, LOAD-indirect reads, a 4-way CMP/BR write-back, a fan-out-8 selector broadcast and an 8-cell demux - 37 cells and 36 hard edges. Reading RFC 8439's schedule as a per-row READ OFFSET instead of the closed form index(k) = 4k + ((j + k*shift) & 3) collapses all of it: row k reads offsets 0,1,2,3 in the column half and k,k+1,k+2,k+3 in the diagonal half, so EVERY ROW TAPS SLOT 0 if it rotates left by one after each quarter round, and the diagonal half is the same walk started k later. The tap becomes a CONSTANT and the permutation becomes a SHIFT REGISTER. 40 cells / 58 plain edges replace 37 cells / 36 hard ones. Proven exact against RFC 8439 S2.3.2 (state AND keystream bytes) and S2.4.2 (the full 114-byte two-block vector) with 8 INV-4 mutants - four of which (diagonal-first, no-realign, reversed spin, stuck tap) still perform exactly 80 invocations, so ONLY A VALUE GATE CATCHES THEM.

MEASURED ON REAL SILICON: the row cell publishing, installing a write-back and rotating (4 spins = identity); INV-48's forwarding rule observed LIVE as a failure then a fix - a cell whose resting face misses its target gives no output AND NO ERROR; and a word transiting cells that have a face but no program at distances 2/3/4/6 - though the build faces bare cells only where a ROUTE claims them, so a gap inside a block's own footprint is still a dead end for an internal WRITE.

NEW INV-51 (renumbered from the builder's INV-50 - third numbering collision this campaign; parallel builders cannot see each other's KB additions): (1) A CLOSED RING TRAPS ITS INTERIOR - nothing emitted inside a ring fold can ever leave, so fold as a serpentine when an interior cell must reach an edge. (2) POSITIONAL PAIRING - build_cell_programs and default_layout must iterate in the SAME ORDER; the cell-id keys HIDE a mismatch and leave whole cells with empty memory. (3) the gap/transit asymmetry above.

IT COMMITTED THE SOURCE THIS TIME, unlike pass 2, and the reasoning is sound: the block builds and is statically green, so the next agent inherits a working toolchain rather than 37 loose cells. It is explicitly marked non-computing in the docstring, the manifest and the lessons log.

THE LESSON IT VOLUNTEERED, which is the best thing in this report: its first fold-search checker credited face flips to cells it had merely NOMINATED, and passed a layout that mis-resolved on silicon. Rewriting it to read MOVE [FACE] out of the actual programs turned three 'green' edges red immediately. 'A MODEL THAT FLATTERS THE DESIGN IS WORSE THAN NO MODEL.' That is the same failure class as the fabricated KB limits this campaign spent a day removing.

ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION: 151 tests pass from main across the keystream golden, the new fixed-tap-ring suite, the QR block and the transit ceiling; manifest honestly needs_human; dashboard clean.

=== PASS 4 (2026-08-30) — THE RING RUNS; INV-50 CLOSED ===

IT WAS CANDIDATE #2 - A FACE THAT MISSES (INV-48 root cause C) - FIVE SEPARATE TIMES. Not a missing HALT, not boot ordering. INV-50 was the accomplice that let all five hide:
  (1) Four cells named the wrong direction outright. One - wbk's row-trigger face NORTH, off the top of the array - WAS the entire 'ring never starts' symptom: wbk had ZERO trace events because wb's jump left on a face with no cell on it.
  (2) THE FACE REGISTER PERSISTS ACROSS ENTRIES. wbk and seq each flipped for one burst and never restored, so the next entry fired in the previous entry's direction.
  (3) A CELL'S FLIP ALSO DEFLECTS WORDS THAT MERELY TRANSIT IT. wb sits on seq's walk and left itself pointing north, so every lap-start trigger bounced back into seq, which re-entered step and ping-ponged. The ring did exactly ONE lap then oscillated forever.
  (4) in0.trig -> in1.default was never declared in internal_jumps at all.
  (5) The router faced tap3 at its adder and sized tap3.q -> in0 at THREE hops instead of one. Every frame reached the collector two words short. THAT ONE EDGE WAS WORTH 75 OF THE 80 LAPS.

PROVEN ON THE REAL PLACED+ROUTED+BUILT CHIP: 80 quarter-round invocations through all sixteen stages, 19 half-boundary realignments, 37/38/39 realignment spins of rows 1/2/3, all four taps armed, and STATE WORD 0 BIT-EXACT AT 0xE4E7F110 - the RFC 8439 S2.3.2 first output word. That is a VALUE gate, not a counting one: four of this cipher's mutants (diagonal-first, no-realign, reversed spin, stuck tap) all still perform exactly 80 invocations.

THE GENERALISABLE MEASUREMENT (now INV-52): over all 233 internal edges, resting-face emits are 211 correct / 0 wrong, but flipped-face emits are 16 correct / 6 wrong - and ALL 16 'correct' are right ONLY BY COINCIDENCE (the resting walk missed, Manhattan fired, and Manhattan happened to match; every one a straight-line hop of 1-2). A resting walk that succeeds SPURIOUSLY is worse than INV-50's fallback because nothing looks anomalous.

INV-50 IS CLOSED, and better than the fix I proposed. I had said to rotate faces by hand; it instead had blocks declare emit_faces() returning a CELL ID, not a direction, so the face is derived from placed coordinates and is orientation-correct BY CONSTRUCTION - which is exactly what the earlier by-hand-rotation attempt got wrong. It also found router._place_block_cells looked programs up by raw positional INDEX, false for every string-keyed block, so those never had their declared fwd_face honoured at all. placekyt/tests 1219 passed (baseline), orientation suite green.

TRAP RECORDED FOR THE NEXT PASS: freeing a word by dropping seq's redundant MOVE half,four FITS AND BREAKS THE BLOCK - shortening seq moves seq.step's entry 15->14 and the build then mis-resolves wbk.back to it instead of row0.pub (also 15). Entry addresses are params-dependent (INV-6/11) and that reaches INTERNAL edges.

METHOD NOTE, sharpening the previous pass's: 'a model that flatters the design is worse than no model' needed a second turn. Reading MOVE [FACE] from real programs is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT - the checker must symbolically execute every path over both branch sides and iterate the face register TO A FIXPOINT. A checker assuming each entry starts clean cannot see defects 2 or 3, i.e. half the bugs.

ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION: 117 tests pass from main; the end-to-end gate genuinely places, auto-routes, builds the bitstream, runs simKYT and reads the trace back (not a proxy); 0xE4E7F110 confirmed against the golden's RFC vector; placekyt/tests 1219 passed with the INV-50 fix applied. INV-52 assigned at landing (the builder correctly left it INV-NEXT).
